title: Streams Simulator Ground Truth v0.1
description: The sealed label for one scenario. Reachable only under the director role; the view struct backing the operator role contains no reference to it. Three onset timestamps rather than one, because the instant a fault becomes true and the instant it becomes knowable are different, and scoring latency against the former punishes a perfect detector for not being clairvoyant.

label.description: The injected fault id, or a negative-class label. Generative, not annotated: there is no annotator to disagree with.

expected_episode.description: False for the negative class. A missing episode on a positive scenario is a mechanism miss producing no model output; it is counted, never silently dropped from the results.

injection_time_ns.description: When the world changed. Taken from the command log. NOT the reference for detection latency.

first_observable_time_ns.description: The earliest instant at which the fault's contribution exceeds the observing channel's noise floor at the declared SNR. Detection before this is classified `suspicious` and triggers a leak investigation, because the only ways to beat the noise floor are luck and cheating. This is the reference for detection latency.

unavoidable_time_ns.description: The instant by which the deviation is large enough that any competent detector must catch it. Detection after this is a miss, however confident the eventual diagnosis. The interval between the two observability timestamps is where the arms actually differ.

observability.description: How the two onset timestamps were computed. The detector is an expression (G-03), so the record carries its form, the channels it reads, and the noise floor after that form's propagation rule — a divergence combines two sigmas in quadrature, a peer residual pools the sibling variance.

effective_sigma.description: The detector's noise floor after propagation. An unrealistically small sigma silently makes every scenario easy, which is why the suppression-effectiveness self-check exists as a cross-check on the world's difficulty.

deadline_ns.description: Present only for domains with a hard physical deadline (aquaculture dissolved-oxygen crash, thermal runaway). Measured from first_observable_time. Past it, the counterfactual consequence occurs regardless of what the runtime concludes.

expected_effector.description: The correct action, for the action-appropriateness loop metric.

trivial_baseline_verdict.description: Output of the audit panel (fixed_threshold, zscore, first_difference, moving_median_residual, channel_silence), each fitted with hindsight on the scenario itself — deliberately unfair to the scenario. A `trivial` scenario is kept as a mechanism regression fixture and excluded from the graded suite: a benchmark a one-line detector wins measures nothing about reasoning.

trivial_baseline_detail.description: Balanced accuracy achieved by each trivial detector. Committed so a reviewer can see which scenarios were excluded and why.

pre_degraded.description: The fault predates t0 and there is no healthy baseline. Counters run-to-failure bias, and exercises the stream's cold-start previous-state handling, which nothing else currently tests.

perturbations.description: Transport perturbations active in this scenario, e.g. 'duplicate_burst@0.02'. Recorded because a miss caused by an injected `drop` is a transport result, not a reasoning result, and the report must be able to say which.

world_state_reference.description: Pointer into world_state_history: the true hidden state over the scenario. Director-only, always. Used for post-hoc analysis of what was actually happening when the model said what it said.
